samples.summary: `snapshot(); batch(no-op)` now leaves a dead undo checkpoint, diverging from YorkieDocStore
samples.evidence: `if (!adopted) this.undoStack.pop();` (memory.ts:298) keeps an adopted checkpoint even when the batch body wrote nothing. So after `snapshot(); batch(() => {})` `canUndo()` is true and the first Cmd+Z restores a byte-identical document (the new test at test/store/memory.test.ts asserts exactly this). Under `YorkieDocStore` the same sequence pushes nothing (`snapshot()` is an empty no-op, yorkie-doc-store.ts:2951, and an empty `doc.update` pushes no change), so `canUndo()` stays false — the two stores answer differently for a shape the store contract (store.ts:62-66, "A batch that writes nothing pushes nothing") says must be identical, and the previous revision's own comment (memory.ts:249) called this the "dead Cmd+Z" it existed to prevent. The shape is reachable: `handleBackspace()` calls `saveSnapshot()` (text-editor.ts:2500) then `deleteSelection()`, whose body can open a unit and write nothing and return false via `if (!normalized) return false;` (text-editor.ts:3942) or `if (!block.tableData) return false;` (text-editor.ts:3948). Contained because the checkpoint is content-equal to the live doc (no data loss) and the next batch re-adopts it, but a user-visible no-op undo press remains.

samples.summary: `willWrite()` runs before the lookups that can throw, so a mutator that fails without writing still destroys the redo stack
samples.evidence: Most mutators call `this.willWrite()` (which does `this.redoStack = []`) as their first statement, before `findBlockInAnyArray()` / `block.tableData!` can throw: e.g. `deleteBlock` (memory.ts:101-103) clears redo and then throws `Block not found: <id>` from findBlockInAnyArray (memory.ts:503); `insertTableRow` (memory.ts:305-307) and the other table mutators clear redo and then throw a TypeError on a non-table block. Nothing was written, yet the redo history is gone. `YorkieDocStore` keeps redo in that case because no change is pushed — the exact parity argument the new doc comment (memory.ts:195-203) uses to justify moving the clear out of `snapshot()`. Note `deleteBlockByIndex` (memory.ts:107-111) and `mergeBlock` (memory.ts:384-388) deliberately validate before `willWrite()`, showing the ordering is inconsistent across the class.

samples.summary: `replaceDocument()` now clears redo, but on YorkieDocStore it is a pure cache sync with no history effect
samples.evidence: `replaceDocument()` gained `this.willWrite()` (memory.ts:62-65). Its contract (store.ts:16-21) is "replace the internal document WITHOUT pushing to the undo stack … sync back after direct Doc mutations", and `YorkieDocStore.replaceDocument()` only refreshes `cachedDoc` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:863-869) — it touches no history, so redo survives there. MemDocStore now throws redo away for the same call. Impact is limited today because no `src` caller remains (grep finds only tests and design docs), but the two stores no longer agree on a method the parity contract covers, and any re-introduced sync-back call would silently kill redo on the in-memory store only.
